# KeyValue

Figma: [04g. KeyValue](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-917) · Family: 04 Data Display · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-03

A label/value pair for lookup-style information - deal details, transaction receipts, contract terms, investor profiles. Label and value have balanced weight (body-text sized, not display) so KeyValue rows compose cleanly in detail panels and don't dominate the page. Two layouts (horizontal for row-style lists, stacked for narrow columns or long values), three sizes, two emphasis levels, optional trailing icon (swappable per instance via the icon prop), bilingual (LTR + RTL). Distinct from Stat (hero KPI, display-scale value) - KeyValue is for information you LOOK UP, not the headline number.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/key-value/reference.png`

### KeyValue

Body-size label and value pair for lookup facts in detail panels and receipts: issuance ID, profit rate, maturity, trustee, transfer reference. Optional trailing icon for info, copy, link or chevron.

Level: molecule · Part of: ActionList

Use when:
- Deal terms panel: profit rate, maturity period, minimum investment
- Transaction or payout receipt rows: amount, date, reference number with copy icon
- Investor profile or KYC details review
- One row with Emphasis=strong for the key financial figure

Don't use when:
- The single hero number on a screen: use Stat
- Multi-column data: use Table / Cell
- Editable fields: use Input or Form Field
- Tappable navigation rows with leading icons: use ListItem

Accessibility: Expose label and value as one readable pair; trailing icon needs its own accessible name (Copy reference).

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

KeyValue presents a label/value pair where the user is looking UP a fact - a deal's issuance ID, a transaction's reference number, a contract's maturity period. The label says what the value is; the value says what it is. Both are body-text-sized so a column of KeyValues reads as a coherent list rather than a series of competing hero KPIs.

This is the deliberate counterpart to Stat. Stat answers "what's the headline number?" with display-scale type. KeyValue answers "what's the detail?" with body text. A deal page might have ONE Stat (Expected return: 12.5%) and a dozen KeyValues underneath (issuance ID, maturity, profit rate, underlying asset, trustee, Sharia advisor, etc).

### Sample detail panel

> **Tip:** When to reach for KeyValue vs Stat: KeyValue is a row of "label: value" information you scan to look something up. Stat is a HERO number on a card or dashboard that demands attention. If you find yourself rendering more than a handful of Stats on one page, most of them probably want to be KeyValues instead.

### Anatomy

A KeyValue is built from at most three elements: a label, a value, and an optional trailing icon. The label tells you what kind of information you're looking at; the value is the information itself; the icon is an affordance for help, copy, expansion, or external navigation.

Label

Short noun phrase identifying what the value is - "Issuance ID", "Profit rate", "Maturity period". Bound to text/muted at Medium weight so it reads as the secondary element (the value is primary). Sized 12-14px depending on the size variant.

Value

The information itself - text, ID, date, number, currency. Bound to text/default. At default emphasis, the value is regular weight at the same size as the label, so they read as a balanced pair. At strong emphasis, the value goes up one size and to semibold to draw the eye.

Trailing icon (optional)

When HasIcon=true, an icon sits after the value. Default is Icon/info (paired with Tooltip for clarification). The icon is INSTANCE_SWAP - swap to Icon/copy-clipboard for IDs/references, Icon/external-link for links, Icon/chevron-right for "tap to expand", Icon/help-circle for "what is this".

### Layout - horizontal vs stacked

Two layouts cover the two real patterns. Horizontal is the default - label left, value right, both on the same line. Stacked puts the label above the value, useful when the value is long or the column is narrow.

Layout = horizontal

Label and value sit on the same line. Use in detail panels and lists where every KeyValue takes one row. The eye scans down the label column on the left and across to the value column on the right.

Layout = stacked

Label sits above the value. Use when (a) the value is too long to fit beside the label in the available width, or (b) the surrounding layout is a narrow column. Less common but cleaner for wordy values.

### Size - sm vs md vs lg

Size picks how much visual real estate each row takes. sm is for dense tables and sidebars where rows are 32px tall. md is the default, comfortable for typical detail panels. lg is for prominent specification sections where each KeyValue should feel substantial.

Size = sm

Padding 6 / row · 12/16 text · 14px icon. Use in dense tables, sidebars, secondary info panels. Reads at 28-32px row height.

Size = md

Padding 8 / row · 13/20 text · 16px icon. DEFAULT. Use in deal detail panels, transaction receipts, profile sections. Reads at 36px row height.

Size = lg

Padding 12 / row · 14/20 text · 18px icon. Use in primary specification sections where each KeyValue should feel like a substantive item. Reads at 44px row height.

### Emphasis - default vs strong

Emphasis lets a single KeyValue inside a long list draw the eye to itself without breaking the visual rhythm. Default emphasis treats label and value as equals in body text. Strong emphasis bumps the value to semibold and one size larger so it reads as the "important" row.

> **Warning:** Use strong emphasis SPARINGLY. The trick works because most rows are default - the strong row is the exception that gets the eye. If you mark three out of six rows as strong, the eye has nowhere to land and the effect breaks down. Pick the one or two values per panel that genuinely deserve more weight.

> **Tip:** If you find yourself wanting strong emphasis on multiple rows, consider whether those rows want to be a Stat (or several Stats) instead. KeyValue with strong emphasis is a halfway point between body text and a hero KPI - useful for one row in a list, not for filling a page with KPIs.

### Trailing icon - affordances

When HasIcon=true, an icon trails the value. The icon's role is contextual - it signals what kind of action or clarification is available. The Figma component defaults to Icon/info; in production code, designers swap it per-instance to match the actual affordance.

### Common icon roles

- Icon/info-circle (default): paired with a Tooltip on hover/focus, used to clarify a value that needs more context. "Profit rate · 12.5% annualized ⓘ" → tooltip explains the calculation basis.
- Icon/help-circle: a clearer "what is this?" affordance. Use for values where the user might not know what they're looking at - "Sharia advisor · ⓘ" with help icon opens an explanation modal.
- Icon/copy-clipboard: for IDs, references, and addresses that users will copy. "Issuance ID · SAF-2025-Q3-014 [copy]". Pair with a success Toast on click.
- Icon/external-link: when the value is a link or the row navigates somewhere. "Trustee · ABC Capital ↗" opens the trustee's entity page.
- Icon/chevron-right: indicates the row is tappable to expand or navigate deeper. Used in mobile detail-list patterns.

> **Warning:** Icon = affordance, not decoration. If the icon doesn't map to an action or clarification the user can take, omit it. A KeyValue with a meaningless icon is more cluttered than one without, even if the icon "looks tidy".

### Direction - LTR + RTL

Every variant exists in LTR (English, IBM Plex Sans) and RTL (Arabic, Noto Sans Arabic). RTL mirrors child order - label is on the right, value sits to its left, trailing icon comes after the value (visually leftmost). Auto-layout handles the flip; designers pick the Direction variant that matches the page.

LTR (English)

RTL (Arabic)

> **Info:** Arabic font fallback (same as Badge, Tooltip, StatusPill, Stat): Noto Sans Arabic for Arabic. IBM Plex Sans Arabic is not installed in this Figma file. If installed later, regenerate all RTL variants.

### Content guidance

KeyValue is body-text-sized, so each row's content has natural length limits. Respect them or the layout breaks.

### Labels

- Short noun phrases. 1-3 words. "Issuance ID", "Maturity period", "Sharia advisor". Not full sentences.
- Sentence case for English: "Issuance ID" not "ISSUANCE ID" or "issuance id".
- Consistent vocabulary across panels. If you call it "Maturity period" on one page, don't call it "Term length" on another.
- Avoid units in the label - "Maturity" with value "18 months", NOT "Maturity (months)" with value "18".

### Values

- Format for human reading, not raw data. "12.5% annualized" not "0.125 per annum". "18 months" not "P18M" or "548 days".
- For SAR currency, use the Riyal icon convention (same as Stat). "1.2M ﷼" not "1.2M SAR".
- For IDs and references, preserve their canonical formatting - "SAF-2025-Q3-014" with the dashes, "SUK-2025-014" without spaces.
- For dates, prefer relative ("2 days ago") when the staleness matters; absolute ("2026-06-03") when precision matters; "Today" / "Yesterday" for very recent.

### When NOT to use KeyValue

- For the headline KPI on a page - that's a Stat. KeyValue is body-text scale; Stat is display scale.
- For interactive content (form fields, toggles, sliders) - those are FormField components.
- For tabular data with multiple columns - that's a Table component. KeyValue is one label/value per row.
- For lists of plain items without labels - that's a List component, not KeyValue with an empty label.

### Code examples - Flutter

Reference implementations. Production code lives in lib/design_system/key_value/.

### Basic usage

```dart
// Minimal - horizontal layout, default emphasis, no icon
SafqahKeyValue(
  label: 'Issuance ID',
  value: 'SAF-2025-Q3-014',
)

// Strong emphasis for an in-list KPI
SafqahKeyValue(
  label: 'Profit rate',
  value: '12.5% annualized',
  emphasis: KeyValueEmphasis.strong,
)

// Trailing icon paired with a tooltip
SafqahKeyValue(
  label: 'Sharia advisor',
  value: 'Shariyah Review Bureau',
  trailingIcon: SyntropyIcons.helpCircle,
  trailingIconAction: () => showTooltip(context, message: 'Independent Sharia advisory board reviewing this issuance.'),
)

// Stacked layout for narrow columns
SafqahKeyValue(
  label: 'Underlying asset',
  value: 'Riyadh commercial complex - Olaya district, north-facing tower',
  layout: KeyValueLayout.stacked,
)

// Copy-to-clipboard interaction
SafqahKeyValue(
  label: 'CMA license',
  value: 'SUK-2025-014',
  trailingIcon: SyntropyIcons.copyClipboard,
  trailingIconAction: () => Clipboard.setData(ClipboardData(text: 'SUK-2025-014')),
)
```

### Detail panel composition

```dart
// Compose multiple KeyValue rows into a detail panel.
// Use SafqahDivider between rows for the scanning rhythm.

class DealDetailPanel extends StatelessWidget {
  final Deal deal;
  const DealDetailPanel({super.key, required this.deal});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final rows = [
      SafqahKeyValue(label: 'Issuance ID', value: deal.id),
      SafqahKeyValue(label: 'Underlying asset', value: deal.underlyingAsset),
      SafqahKeyValue(
        label: 'Profit rate',
        value: '${deal.profitRate}% annualized',
        emphasis: KeyValueEmphasis.strong,
      ),
      SafqahKeyValue(label: 'Maturity period', value: '${deal.maturityMonths} months'),
      SafqahKeyValue(label: 'Sharia advisor', value: deal.shariaAdvisor),
      SafqahKeyValue(
        label: 'CMA license',
        value: deal.cmaLicense,
        trailingIcon: SyntropyIcons.copyClipboard,
        trailingIconAction: () => Clipboard.setData(ClipboardData(text: deal.cmaLicense)),
      ),
    ];

    return Column(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
      children: [
        for (int i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) ...[
          rows[i],
          if (i < rows.length - 1) const SafqahDivider(),
        ],
      ],
    );
  }
}
```

### Variant resolution

```dart
// File: lib/design_system/key_value/safqah_key_value.dart
class SafqahKeyValue extends StatelessWidget {
  final String label;
  final String value;
  final KeyValueLayout layout;
  final KeyValueSize size;
  final KeyValueEmphasis emphasis;
  final IconData? trailingIcon;
  final VoidCallback? trailingIconAction;

  const SafqahKeyValue({
    super.key,
    required this.label,
    required this.value,
    this.layout = KeyValueLayout.horizontal,
    this.size = KeyValueSize.md,
    this.emphasis = KeyValueEmphasis.default_,
    this.trailingIcon,
    this.trailingIconAction,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final theme = SyntropyTheme.of(context);
    final spec = size.resolveSpec();
    final valueWeight = emphasis == KeyValueEmphasis.strong
      ? FontWeight.w600
      : FontWeight.w400;
    final valueSize = emphasis == KeyValueEmphasis.strong
      ? spec.valueStrongSize
      : spec.valueSize;

    final labelWidget = Text(label, style: TextStyle(
      fontSize: spec.labelSize,
      height: spec.labelLh / spec.labelSize,
      fontWeight: FontWeight.w500,
      color: theme.text.muted,
    ));
    final valueWidget = Text(value, style: TextStyle(
      fontSize: valueSize,
      fontWeight: valueWeight,
      color: theme.text.default_,
    ));

    final children = <Widget>[valueWidget];
    if (trailingIcon != null) {
      children.add(SizedBox(width: 6));
      children.add(Semantics(
        button: trailingIconAction != null,
        label: trailingIconAction != null ? '$trailingIcon for $label' : null,
        child: GestureDetector(
          onTap: trailingIconAction,
          child: Icon(trailingIcon, size: spec.iconSize),
        ),
      ));
    }

    return layout == KeyValueLayout.horizontal
      ? Row(
          mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.spaceBetween,
          children: [labelWidget, Row(mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min, children: children)],
        )
      : Column(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: [labelWidget, Row(mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min, children: children)],
        );
  }
}
```

### Do and Don't

Five pairs of operational guidance for KeyValue usage.

### One label-value pair per KeyValue

- **Do** · Scenario name: Render each fact as its own KeyValue. "Issuance ID · SAF-2025-Q3-014" is one KeyValue; "Profit rate · 12.5%" is another. Stack them with dividers between.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't cram multiple facts into one row ("Issuance · SAF-2025-Q3-014 · 18 months · 12.5%"). If you have several facts, you have several KeyValues.

### Use strong emphasis sparingly

- **Do** · Scenario name: One or two strong rows per panel maximum, on the KPIs that genuinely matter to the user's decision - profit rate, target amount, maturity.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't make every row strong. If everything is emphasized, nothing is. The strong row works because most are default - it's the contrast that draws the eye.

### Match emphasis to importance

- **Do** · Scenario name: Use strong for the financial-decision KPI inside a list of metadata - "Profit rate · 12.5% annualized" deserves emphasis next to "Trustee · ABC Capital".
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't use strong on metadata or housekeeping fields ("Created at", "Last modified"). The user isn't scanning the list for those.

### KeyValue vs Stat

- **Do** · Scenario name: KeyValue is body-text scale for lookup-style information in detail panels. Stat is display-scale for hero KPIs on dashboards. Pick based on what the user is doing - looking up vs. seeing at a glance.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't render 6 Stats on a deal detail page when you mean 6 KeyValues with one strong row. Multiple Stats fight for attention; KeyValues compose into a coherent list.

### Icon = affordance

- **Do** · Scenario name: Add a trailing icon when there's a real action - copy, expand, link out, tooltip-explain. Pick the icon that matches the action (copy-clipboard for IDs, external-link for links, etc).
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't add a default info icon to every KeyValue "for tidiness". An icon without an action is visual debt; users learn to ignore it, which weakens the icons that DO have actions.

### Notes from the maintainer

Design decisions, known gaps, and constraints for the next maintainer.

> **Info:** Label and value are TEXT component properties (label#... and value#...). Designers override the strings per-instance via Figma's instance properties panel - no need to detach. The defaults are the size-appropriate sample strings ("Profit rate" / "12.5% annualized" for md).

> **Info:** The icon is INSTANCE_SWAP with default info-circle. Designers swap to copy-clipboard, external-link, help-circle, chevron-right, etc per the action context. This is the same pattern as Tooltip and StatusPill - central swap property, per-instance override.

> **Info:** No separator/divider built into KeyValue. To divide rows in a detail panel, drop a Divider (04h) between KeyValue instances. Keeping the separator out of the KeyValue component itself means the spacing math is simpler and Divider stays the single source of truth for visual dividers.

> **Tip:** Horizontal layouts use primaryAxisAlignItems=MIN, not SPACE_BETWEEN. That means a KeyValue at its natural size shows label and value next to each other with the configured rowGap between them. To get label-left + value-right behavior in a panel, set the KeyValue instance to Fill container width when placed inside a vertical auto-layout column - the SPACE_BETWEEN happens at the container level, not the KeyValue level. This trade-off keeps the component content-sized by default.

> **Info:** Strong emphasis bumps the value to semibold AND one size up (sm 12→13, md 13→14, lg 14→16). The size bump is what makes the emphasis feel substantive without overwhelming - a weight change alone is often too subtle on small text.

> **Info:** No dark mode yet. KeyValue has Light-mode-only bindings (same as Badge, Tooltip, StatusPill, Stat). The semantic tokens it binds to (text/default, text/muted, border/subtle) have dark mode definitions, so adding dark mode is mostly verification.

> **Info:** Arabic font fallback: Noto Sans Arabic. IBM Plex Sans Arabic is not installed in this Figma file. If installed later, regenerate all RTL variants. (Same constraint as Badge, Tooltip, StatusPill, Stat.)

> **Warning:** Don't detach KeyValue instances to customize the trailing icon - use the icon INSTANCE_SWAP property. To customize the label or value, use the label and value TEXT properties. Detached instances break design system audit.
